subject: Science
summary: Light travels in straight lines. Reflection occurs at polished surfaces following laws of reflection. Curved spherical mirrors (concave and convex) form real or virtual images governed by the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and magnification m = -v/u. Refraction is the bending of light across media governed by Snell's law (sin i / sin r = n). Lenses form images following 1/v - 1/u = 1/f with power P = 1/f (m) in Dioptres.

pages.heading: 1. Nature of Light & Laws of Reflection
notes: • Light is electromagnetic radiation that enables vision and travels in straight lines.
• Law 1: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection (∠i = ∠r).
• Law 2: Incident ray, normal at point of incidence, and reflected ray all lie in the same plane.
• Spherical Mirrors: Concave (reflecting inwards, converging) vs Convex (reflecting outwards, diverging).

spokenLines.text: Welcome to class! Today we master one of the most scoring chapters in Class 10 Physics: Light — Reflection and Refraction.
Light always travels in straight lines, and when it strikes any polished surface, it obeys two strict laws.
The angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection, and all rays lie in the exact same plane.
For spherical mirrors, concave mirrors curve inward to converge light, while convex mirrors curve outward to diverge it.

pages.heading: 2. Ray Geometry & Image Formation in Motion

spokenLines.text: Watch closely as we trace the rays onto a concave mirror.
Parallel incoming rays bounce off the curved mirror surface and converge directly through the principal focus.
Notice where the rays intersect: a real, inverted image forms right in front of the mirror.
Now interact with the live ray diagram on the board.
Drag the object from infinity towards the mirror. Notice how the image moves further away and grows larger.
When you place the object between the focus and the pole, the image suddenly turns virtual and erect behind the mirror!
Look at the 3D lens model on the board. You can drag and rotate it in 3D space.
As parallel light beams enter the curved glass boundary, each ray refracts towards the optical axis.
All refracted rays meet at the focal point, demonstrating why a convex lens is a converging lens.

pages.heading: 5. Essential Exam Formulas & Sign Conventions
notes: • Snell's Law of Refraction: sin i / sin r = constant = n₂₁ (Refractive Index)
• Absolute Refractive Index: n = c / v  (where c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
• Lens Formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f  |  Lens Power: P = 1/f(in meters) [Unit: Dioptre, D]

spokenLines.text: Here is your high-yield formula cheat-sheet for board exams.
Remember: Mirror formula has a plus sign: 1 over v plus 1 over u equals 1 over f.
Lens formula has a minus sign: 1 over v minus 1 over u equals 1 over f.
And Snell's law proves the ratio of sine i to sine r is always constant.

practice.title: NCERT End of Chapter Interactive Practice

questions.question: The relationship between focal length (f) and radius of curvature (R) for a spherical mirror of small aperture is R = _____.
questions.explanation: Radius of curvature is twice the focal length of a spherical mirror (R = 2f).

questions.question: The SI unit of power of a lens with focal length in meters is called _____.
questions.explanation: Power P = 1/f(m) and its SI unit is dioptre (D). 1 D = 1 m⁻¹.

questions.question: Which of the following mirrors is used by dentists to see an enlarged image of teeth?
questions.explanation: When an object is placed between the pole (P) and focus (F) of a concave mirror, it forms an erect, magnified, virtual image.

questions.question: A ray of light traveling from air enters obliquely into water. The light ray will:
questions.explanation: Water is optically denser than air. Light slows down in water, hence bends towards the normal.

questions.question: Magnification produced by a convex mirror is always less than 1 (m < 1) and positive.
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image behind the mirror.
